info.title: meshy/remesh
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "meshy/remesh", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: Request body for Meshy's remesh operation (docs.meshy.ai/en/api/remesh): re-topologise or re-format an existing mesh. Supply exactly one of input_task_id or model_url; Meshy requires no single field, so the only structural narrowing is that an empty body is refused.

convert_format_only.description: If true, only changes the format of the input model file, ignoring other inputs like topology, resize_height, and target_polycount.

input_task_id.description: The ID of the completed Image to 3D or Text to 3D task you wish to remesh. Required if model_url is not provided.

model_url.description: A publicly accessible URL or data URI to a 3D model. Supported formats glb, gltf, obj, fbx, stl. Required if input_task_id is not provided.

resize_height.description: Resize the model to a certain height measured in meters. 0 means no resizing.

target_formats.description: A list of target formats for the remeshed model.

target_polycount.description: Specify the target number of polygons in the generated model. Valid range is 100 to 300,000.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for Meshy's remesh operation: the terminal `GET /proxy/meshy/openapi/v1/remesh/{task_id}` task document, forwarded unchanged. The operation is SUBMIT-AND-POLL — `POST /proxy/meshy/openapi/v1/remesh` answers a `MeshyRemeshCreateResponse` handle whose `result` is the task id and which carries no mesh, and Router polls on the caller's behalf — so the body a caller receives is the finished task document rather than that handle.
`meshy/remesh` names an OPERATION rather than a model version. It re-meshes a mesh the caller already has (identified in the request by a preceding task's id or by a model URL), so it consumes a 3D asset and produces a 3D asset; it is not one of the text-to-3D generations `meshy/meshy-5`, `meshy/meshy-6` and `meshy/meshy-7` name.
The remeshed model is in `model_urls`, at whichever of `glb`, `fbx`, `obj`, `usdz`, `blend` and `stl` the request's `target_formats` asked for — which of them are populated depends on the request, so read the one that is present rather than keying completion off `glb` alone. Comfy Router draws that line: a `SUCCEEDED` task carrying no mesh URL at all is answered as a Comfy Router error rather than with this document, so through Router a `200` here always carries a mesh — but not always the same one. The line is drawn by `classifyMeshy`, which is shared with the text-to-3D family and accepts a seventh leaf, `model_urls.pre_remeshed_glb`, that this operation's `MeshyRemeshModelUrls` does not declare; a task carrying only that key would be forwarded rather than refused.
`status` is Meshy's own UPPERCASE vocabulary, forwarded unchanged and not case-folded. This operation's enum is `PENDING`, `PROCESSING`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED` — note `PROCESSING` where the text-to-3D family says `IN_PROGRESS`, and no `CANCELED`. `SUCCEEDED` is the one terminal success; `FAILED` is a terminal failure and reaches a Router caller as a Comfy Router error with Meshy's own reason in `task_error.message`. `progress` runs 0..100 and is 100 on a succeeded task. `preceding_tasks` is only meaningful while `PENDING`, which a Router caller never sees.

MeshyRemeshModelUrls.description: Downloadable URLs to the remeshed 3D model files.

blend.description: Downloadable URL to the Blender file.

fbx.description: Downloadable URL to the FBX file.

glb.description: Downloadable URL to the GLB file.

obj.description: Downloadable URL to the OBJ file.

stl.description: Downloadable URL to the STL file.

usdz.description: Downloadable URL to the USDZ file.

created_at.description: Timestamp of when the task was created, in milliseconds.

finished_at.description: Timestamp of when the task was finished, in milliseconds. 0 if not finished.

preceding_tasks.description: The count of preceding tasks. Only meaningful when status is PENDING.

progress.description: Progress of the task. 0 if not started, 100 when succeeded.

started_at.description: Timestamp of when the task was started, in milliseconds. 0 if not started.

MeshyTaskError.description: Error object that contains the error message if the task failed.

MeshyTopology.description: Specify the topology of the generated model.
